interpretation.text: K-means clustering of 150 cases on 4 variables produced 3 clusters of sizes 50, 53, 47. The clusters accounted for 76.7% of the total variance, and the average silhouette width of 0.46 indicates a weak cluster structure.

title: K-Means Clustering
code:
library(ggnext)
# K-means clustering with k = 3: sepal_length, sepal_width, petal_length, petal_width
vars <- c("sepal_length", "sepal_width", "petal_length", "petal_width")
d <- data[complete.cases(data[, vars, drop = FALSE]), , drop = FALSE]
x <- scale(d[vars])   # z-scores, so every variable counts equally
set.seed(123)
km <- kmeans(x, centers = 3, nstart = 25, iter.max = 100)
cluster <- factor(km$cluster)
sizes <- data.frame(cluster = levels(cluster), n = as.vector(table(cluster)))
centers <- aggregate(d[vars], list(cluster = cluster), mean)
sil <- cluster::silhouette(as.integer(cluster), dist(x))
silhouette_avg <- mean(sil[, "sil_width"])
sizes$silhouette <- as.vector(tapply(sil[, "sil_width"], cluster, mean))
sizes$withinss <- km$withinss
pc <- prcomp(x)
plot_df <- data.frame(PC1 = pc$x[, 1], PC2 = pc$x[, 2], cluster = cluster)
pc_var <- round(100 * pc$sdev^2 / sum(pc$sdev^2), 1)
p_clusters <- ggnext(plot_df, aes(PC1, PC2, color = cluster)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(title = "Clusters on the first two principal components") +
  theme_modern()
p_clusters <- p_clusters + labs(x = paste0("PC1 (", pc_var[1], "%)"), y = paste0("PC2 (", pc_var[2], "%)"))
# Total within-cluster sum of squares for k = 1 to 10
k_max <- min(10, nrow(unique(x)) - 1)
set.seed(123)
elbow <- data.frame(k = seq_len(k_max), wss = sapply(seq_len(k_max), function(k) kmeans(x, k, nstart = 25, iter.max = 100)$tot.withinss))
p_elbow <- ggnext(elbow, aes(k, wss)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 3, dash = "4 4") +
  labs(title = "Elbow plot", x = "Number of clusters (k)", y = "Total within-cluster sum of squares") +
  theme_modern()
